Stock C8 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Drags Modded Z06 at Famoso Dragstrip, It's Over in 10.66s
9 photos
Photo: Daniel Dolofan / YouTube
Someone was lucky enough to catch a skirmish that flew under the radar of big YouTubers. This guy, meanwhile, has less than 500 subscribers but still manages to give us some quality content – at least if you’re a C8 enthusiast .
The C8 Chevrolet Corvette has been around since 2019 and went on sale in 2020, with the base Stingray model packing up to 495 hp thanks to its 6.2-liter naturally aspirated V8 engine. The mid-engine setup was the main novelty for the new iteration at the time of release, but that was just the preamble.
Team Corvette continued to put into production one major idea after another. They brought to market the Z06 homologation version for the race model, complete with a new 5.5-liter NA V8 that churns out 670 hp via its flat-plane crankshaft configuration, and also achieved a world record in the process.
Then came the first-ever performance hybrid in the form of the E-Ray, a Stingray-based model featuring the same V8 but also an electrified system to boost power up to 655 horsepower while also making it the first all-wheel drive Corvette in history. Of course, Chevrolet didn’t stop there, and they quickly rocked the supercar world with twins: ZR1 and ZR1X.
Those have no less than 1,064 hp or 1,250 hp when electrified via their twin-turbo V8s and electric aids. Now, the Corvette has also gone through a mid-cycle refresh procedure, which brought out a new interior for the 2026 model year and then also a new base 6.7-litr V8 engine for the 2027 model year alongside the new Grand Sport and Grand Sport X models.
But that doesn’t mean the ‘older’ versions are suddenly obsolete. Here’s an example, of course, courtesy of an unknown videographer that caught a modded C8 Chevy Corvette Z06 going up against a stock E-Ray at Famoso Dragstrip . By the way, the Famoso Bakersfield Raceway dragstrip is located in McFarland, California, just north of Bakersfield, California, and it’s the historical venue for the annual March Meet, also known as the U.S. Fuel and Gas Championships.
On this occasion, the quarter-mile dragstrip was ripe for the taking for these two Corvettes, one being a Z06 with full bolt-on, a stock tune, an aftermarket straight pipe exhaust, a cold air intake, and lighter alloy wheels. The other is a stock E-Ray, the white example, and it was a pretty interesting setup.
Well, as it turns out, this race was decided from the very beginning, as one of the drivers had a faster reaction time and took advantage of that to distance themselves from their adversary. The latter tried to engage in a pursuit and make a spectacular comeback, but it was all futile – it was all over in 10.66s at 126 mph, while the runner-up posted a 10.98s at 128 mph. Come on, now, let’s see who’s who!

Chevrolet Corvette Z06X Would Cost ZR1 Money, Says Corvette Chief Engineer Tony Roma
6 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
The Corvette's order guide has never been this crowded. Six distinct variants are now available to configure for the 2027 model year, starting with the LS6-engined Stingray. At the other end of the spectrum, the ZR1 with the electrified front axle of the Grand Sport X is known as the ZR1X and starts at $227,800 before DFC.
One cell in the matrix sits empty, though, and that cell is the Z06X. As per Corvette chief engineer Tony Roma, such a car would make sense only if priced similarly to the already expensive ZR1. As of this writing, the non-hybrid twin of the ZR1X will set you back a cool $198,000 sans destination freight charge.
Roma spent an hour on The Drivecast answering a question that certain Corvette enthusiasts have already settled in their own heads. Roma claims that his team at General Motors could easily put the pieces together to deliver the Z06X, but alas, the company is not committed to making it happen anytime soon.
Every C8-generation Corvette carries an open cavity between the front wheels, a bay GM has filled since the E-Ray came to be with the LT2 small block of the Stingray and an electrified front axle that was later transplanted into the ZR1X. What used to be the central tunnel on C7- and previous-gen Corvettes serves as the home of the high-voltage battery in the 2027 model year Grand Sport X (which replaces the E-Ray) and the ZR1X.
Swapping in the Grand Sport X's 6.7-liter small block for the flat-plane engine of the Z06 would result in a parts-bin maximum output in the neighborhood of 860 horsepower, putting the Z06X slightly above the 721-pony Grand Sport X in the range. Tony Roma's hesitation in regard to the Z06X is best viewed as financial rather than theoretical, yet his math doesn't add up.
Photo: General Motors "It would have to end up being almost ZR1 money," he said on The Drivecast. Let's dig in a little first. As opposed to $198,000 from the outset for the combustion-only ZR1, the ZR1X is $29,800 pricier. Similarly, the Grand Sport X is $110,000 before taxes and options, making it $23,700 more expensive than the gas-only Grand Sport.
Given that a brand-new Z06 presently retails at $121,800 in the Detroit-based automaker's home market, the Z06X would theoretically be no more than $30,000 pricier, landing in at $151,800 before anything instead of nearly $200,000 for the ZR1. That's nearly fifty grand off Roma's estimate, but alas, we're not the peeps in charge of pricing at GM.
The gap, however, does have reasons. An electrified Z06 would be a properly niche low-volume special, and amortizing development costs over a thin pool is the main reason why our crude match does not make financial sense to General Motors . Parking it near the ZR1 would also trigger the effect Porsche exploited with the 992.1-phase 911 Turbo S and Turbo.
While the gap between the Turbo S and Turbo runs thin, buyers are willing to spend extra for the S version, making the plain one an easy allocation. Pricing the Z06X in ZR1 territory would result in two Corvette models battling for the same customer, hurting each other in the process.
"Maybe in the future, we'll decide that [Z06X] is an entry worthy of the investment," concluded Roma about the oft-rumored Z06 with electrified all-wheel drive.

BMW Is Paying Insane Money To Get 8,000 Employees Gone by the End of 2027
12 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW just closed the counter on its German layoff program, the reason being too many takers. The Munich-based automaker needs 8,000 white collars out the door by the end of 2027, so it emailed severance offers to tens of thousands of staff. Roughly 40,000 people logged in to see what their exit was actually worth, and curiously enough, the internal HR portal folded within hours.
As per German publication Handelsblatt, the fix landed the next day, and the applications kept stacking higher and higher. A few days later, BMW stopped taking new ones altogether so it could process the queue. When a cost-cutting program develops a waiting list, chances are the company does not have a persuasion problem anymore. Instead, a triage problem arises.
What's pulling those applicants in line? As reported by Handelsblatt, which is citing insiders, individual dealers are clearing 650,000 euros. That puts BMW above Mercedes and Volkswagen. The latter, which is the largest German and European manufacturer of them all, topped out near 405,000 euros two years ago, devoid of an early-bird premium.
Over at Merc, long-serving team leads were paid around half a million euros last year. BMW seemingly read the market, then bolted on the so-called Turbo Bonus for anyone who agrees to take the early exit. The offer itself hands subject employees two doors out, specifically March 31 of 2027 or October 31 of 2027. The early doors pay extra, and the program dies at the end of that October no matter what happens until then.
Handelsblatt understands the math runs on an individual basis under uniform principles. BMW , however, understandably refused to comment on concrete figures. The manufacturer's generosity should not be viewed as a poisoned chalice, but as cold-blooded bookkeeping. Cutting those 8,000 positions by the end of next year will bank the company around one billion euros per year from 2028.
Photo: BMW Simply put, writing comically large checks now helps BMW write fewer payroll checks in the near future. Of course, there are a few ways to take the money offered by the Munich-based manufacturer.
Employees are offered installments, one lump sum, part of the negotiated sum into the company's pension pot, part into a direct insurance, or any blend of the aforementioned. BMW is also happy to include a well-wishing qualified reference letter, if the applicant asks for one.
Turning 55 before the program ends, the employee counts as a retiree for certain extras, employee conditions on new and used cars included. The company car clause is especially interesting. Anyone leaving can buy their last service car in the month their contract ends, and senior pay grades can walk out with two such vehicles. Looking at the bigger picture, it's no wonder BMW had to make quitting irresistible during these incredibly difficult of times.
The hurry behind all of this comes from the most recent of sales charts, with China being the automaker's biggest oof right now. BMW sales in the PRC dropped by almost 25 percent in the last quarter, while growth in Europe and the US could not plug the China-shaped hole in the Q3 2026 sales report.
Via // Handelsblatt

Antilia Is a Sculptural Yacht Concept With Generous Open-Air Areas and Three Jacuzzis
18 photos
Photo: Baran Akalin Design
For visionary sea lovers looking to invest in an avant-garde superyacht, the best designs are those that are ready to transition from aspirational blueprint to reality. Turkish shipyard KRC Yachting has just unveiled one such design in the form of the Antilia superyacht concept.
Developed in collaboration with Baran Akalın Design, this ready-to-build concept blends an architectural exterior with spacious living areas and a restrained approach to luxury.
Measuring 43 meters (141 feet) long, Antilia is designed to offer comfort and flexibility for extended stays at sea. It boasts a massive beach club with transforming balconies at the water’s edge, three separate Jacuzzis, and a huge upper-deck owner’s cabin. According to the designers, the concept is ready for production, with construction estimated to take 24 months.
The vessel’s imposing profile is mainly due to a sculpted hull with clean architectural lines and impressive yet carefully-proportioned volumes. The designers intentionally avoided visual complexity or excessive ornamentation, relying on bold shapes, like angular geometric chamfers rather than traditional soft curves or 90-degree edges. Expansive, heavily tinted bands of glass wrap around the hull and superstructure, and a dramatic forward-sweeping line bridges the main deck and upper decks, creating a strong sense of motion even when the yacht is at anchor.
Photo: Baran Akalin Design Like most modern concepts, the Antilia is designed around life at sea, so open air areas abound on board. Large, strategically positioned openings allow for a seamless indoor-outdoor flow, blurring the lines between interior living areas and al-fresco spaces.
The generous beach club perfectly exemplifies this seamless flow. Here, opening balconies extend the beach club into a water-edge living space that blends indoor comfort with direct sea views. From the swimming platform, a pair of illuminated stairs lead to a raised seating area that provides a comfortable place to relax while enjoying the surrounding vistas. The beach club also features one of the yacht’s three Jacuzzis, with the other two positioned on the upper deck and flybridge.
Speaking of the flybridge, this elevated area comprises a bar for relaxed drinks, a shaded lounge, and sunbathing space aft. Guests have other lounging options as well. One of them is located aft of the main saloon, allowing guests to easily move between indoor and outdoor spaces.
Photo: Baran Akalin Design With a beam of 8.55 meters (28 feet) and a draft of 2.4 meters (8 feet), Antilia 43 superyacht has a gross tonnage of 498 GT. In terms of interior layout, the designers proposed an eight-stateroom arrangement, with space for up to twelve guests. For the owner, they envisioned a luxurious suite on the upper deck, complete with a private balcony on the upper terrace. The suite can also be accessed via a staircase from the main deck.
As for the convivial areas, the spacious salon on the main deck includes a lounge with plush seating and a dining area, and it seamlessly connects with the outdoor seating areas as well. Antilia’s interior spaces will be finished with natural textures and materials to create a warm, inviting ambiance.
Photo: Baran Akalin Design Both the choice of materials and spatial configuration are meant to contribute to visual continuity and a sense of calm and serenity. Of course, prospective owners are free to personalize the interior configuration, furnishings, finishes, and decorative details to suit their preferences.
The yacht concept also features a tender garage and a gym, both of them located beneath the beach club and both customizable to the owner’s requirements.
In terms of propulsion, the Antilia motor yacht will be powered by two MAN D2868 LE436 engines, each producing 1,200 horsepower. The yacht is expected to reach a top speed of 14 knots and cruise at 12 knots.

source_document.body:
The U.S. Navy has taken some heat recently for focusing too heavily on the Middle East and neglecting the Asia-Pacific. The same cannot be said of the U.S. Marine Corps , which unveiled a new strategy in 2019 relying on dispersed groups of Marines to wield drones and anti-ship missiles in archipelagic warfare in order to unhinge Chinese maritime expansion. As the Marines are developing new capabilities at the pointy end of the American spear, so to speak, it’s not surprising that USMC strategy is attracting lots of attention from Chinese defense experts. This article summarizes several recent Chinese-language assessments.
The close attention that Beijing is paying to the new USMC strategy became clear about a year ago when the Global Times [环球时报] published an unusual editorial decrying Washington’s new determination to deploy anti-ship missiles proximate to China. Arguing that the new American strategy aims to correct a U.S. Navy prioritization for “open ocean control” rather than “close-quarters engagement in confined waters,” this article concludes that Washington’s effort to “control maritime chokepoints [aims to] curtail the freedom of rivals to operate at sea … [and] introduces new risks … .”
A much more detailed study of the new USMC strategy appeared in early 2025 in the naval magazine Modern Ships [现代舰船]. This Chinese assessment noted with considerable alarm that the USMC was experimenting with unmanned surface vessels capable of firing the stealthy LRASM anti-ship cruise missile and that these units could alternatively serve as forward scouts, fixing targets for long-range U.S. military fires. Still, this analysis underlines some weaknesses of the USMC strategy, including the range limitations of related sensors and drones, and even characterized the air-defense capabilities of the USMC as “precarious.” Another study in this same magazine had earlier drawn attention to the logistics quandaries raised by the new strategy.
A 2026 Chinese analysis in another Chinese navy-affiliated magazine, Shipborne Weapons [舰载武器], offers a sharper critique of the Marines’ new approach, noting that the creation of the Marine Littoral Regiments (MLR) “actually represents campaign preparation by the USMC to militarily intervene in China’s unification.” At the outset, this study notes that many American think tanks raised doubts about the strategy, suggesting that forward bases without sea and air control could prove “untenable.”
There is a recognition in this analysis that the new mobile missile launchers that are being deployed by the USMC are small, light, and thus “not easily discovered by … surveillance.” In the end, this study concludes that the USMC strategy is vulnerable because the “U.S has no way to quickly establish air superiority. This could take weeks or months and would entail massive losses.”
Among the most remarkable pieces written by Chinese experts on the new USMC direction is one that was published in translation recently by the China institute at U.S. Naval War College (NWC). That translation deserves extra attention due to the fact that it was written by senior active-duty Chinese Navy officers and also because it was published originally in a sensitive internal circulation Chinese military journal too.
Though this piece does not touch directly on the sensitive Taiwan issue, and it also explicitly notes the USMC strategy aims at deterrence of Beijing, it nevertheless explains that the new USMC deployments amount to “continuous penetration and encroachment into our near seas” and argues that China must “establish effective countermeasures.” Notably, this high-level rendering links the USMC strategy to China’s improving submarine force in significant detail, observing that forward deployed Marine forces could deploy “hydro-acoustic arrays and other assets to establish barrier zones and monitoring areas to track Chinese submarine operations.” Similar arguments are made that U.S. deployments could degrade Chinese air defenses by employing drone swarms “to overwhelm our radar tracking capacity.”
The Chinese Navy authors caution against applying resource-intensive assets to defeat such American asymmetric tactics. However, the conclusion of the article is rather disturbing since it argues that China must counter this posture by deploying a Chinese “proactive offensive posture, aggressively expand[ing] our operational reach, [and] project[ing] forces forward.” Elaborating, they counsel: “We must maintain and normalize forward-deployed forces, extend[ing] undersea combat capabilities as far forward as feasible.”
This conclusion and other aspects of these Chinese-language analyses raise some rather uncomfortable questions for U.S. defense planners. The final translation done by NWC strongly hints that the Chinese Navy may be adopting a more aggressive approach as a direct reaction to the forward lean in American strategy. This seems to be a very clear manifestation of the so-called ‘security dilemma,’ wherein two powers’ defensive measures develop into a dangerous escalatory spiral. Moreover, there is a clear recognition by Chinese strategists that forward USMC elements could be vulnerable due to logistics challenges and lack of proper air and missile defenses. It would not be the first time that the USMC was deployed haphazardly in East Asia at the cost of many American lives.
Understanding these dynamics, American leaders should recalibrate and opt to rely less on forward defense. Alternatively, the USMC should aim to embrace the strategic depth of the Pacific and its myriad island archipelagos (e.g. the Philippines) in a less costly, less risky, more sustainable, and clearly defensive strategy.
Lyle Goldstein is director of the China Initiative at Brown University’s Watson School and concurrently serves as director of the Asia Program at the think-tank Defense Priorities.

Second Crew of Mars Astronauts NASA Locked Up for a Year Are Coming Out on October 31
7 photos
Photo: NASA
On October 19, 2025, American space agency NASA locked up four people inside a 3D-printed habitat located at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas. More than a year later, the crew is preparing to come back to civilization.
The moment marks the end of the second of three Mars simulation missions, and another step taken toward a better understanding of what a crewed mission to the Red Planet will require. The first one, performed by Kelly Haston, Ross Brockwell, Nathan Jones, and Anca Selariu, ended in July 2024, after 378 days of isolation.
The crew of the second mission comprises Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, Matthew Montgomery, and James Spicer. The four people stepped inside the so-called Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) facility, tasked with pretty much the same things as their predecessors.
CHAPEA , a 1,700-square-foot habitat created by a company called ICON, is also called Mars Duna Alpha, and is described as the highest-fidelity simulated habitat our species has ever constructed.
Its role is to completely isolate groups of people from the outside world for long periods of time, with the goal of informing NASA on what it would take for a long-duration mission to another world to succeed.
The second CHAPEA crew spent the past year doing all the things Mars astronauts would have to do, including doing science, performing Mars walks, making ends meet with limited resources, growing crops, and coping with communication delays of up to 45 minutes each way.
When they come out at the end of the month, the crew will have spent 378 days inside. Soon after, NASA will conduct a two-week-long post-mission evaluation and debrief program, trying to gather as much data as possible on the experience, but also on crew health and performance.
The CHAPEA program was first announced back in 2021, and it is supposed to be three missions long. It’s not clear at this time when the next group of four people will go inside the facility for the final year-long mission.
If by chance you intend to be a part of that, keep in mind that there are certain conditions that must be met. They include being a U.S. citizen or permanent resident aged between 30 and 55 years old, healthy, and non-smoking.
When it comes to skills and qualifications, NASA requires a master's degree from an accredited institution in a STEM field, two or more years of professional experience in a STEM field, or, in its place, at least 1,000 hours as pilot-in-command on jet aircraft.
CHAPEA is not the only habitat designed to simulate living conditions on other worlds. For years, people have been going to Antarctica or the International Space Station (ISS) to do that, or they’ve entered another facility located at the Johnson Space Center: the Human Exploration Research Analog (HERA). Even the European Space Agency (ESA) has one, the Future Lunar Exploration Habitat (FLEXHab).

Aircraft Carrier Sailing in the Pacific Takes Control of Refuelling Drone 2K Miles Away in Illinois
23 photos
Photo: U.S. Navy
About a month ago, in mid-September, the U.S. Navy announced it has decided to give the Boeing-made MQ-25A Stingray drone the role of an uncrewed aerial refuelling tanker, the first time in the history of the world that such an aircraft is used in such a capacity. And it didn’t take long for the military branch to give us a taste of how that decision could reshape the future of naval aviation operations.
The Stingray has been in the works for a while now, and it was initially designed to fulfil the same roles most other drones of this size fulfill. You know, stuff like intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance (ISR), and strike missions.
Although those capabilities are still on the table, someone, somewhere, decided it would be a good idea to use it as an airborne refuelling tanker, and the Navy immediately saw the merits of that. Hence, the $562 million contract Boeing got back in September to deliver three MQ-25A Stingray aerial refuelling drones starting in 2029.
Until that happens, the aerospace giant and the Navy are hard at work putting the design through its paces. The latest gimmick is having one of these drones controlled by people located on the deck of an aircraft carrier, thousands of miles away.
The carrier in question is the Nimitz-class USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76), which is presently on duty somewhere in the Pacific Ocean. From there, in what the Navy calls a historic U.S. naval aviation event, the ship was able to take control of and command an MQ-25A located at Boeing's facility in Mascoutah, Illinois.
According to the available info, the distance between the two was, at the time the exercise was conducted, 2,100 miles (3,380 km). To make the connection work, Reagan’s Unmanned Air Warfare Center (UAWC) employed an MD-5C Ground Control Station and a series of low-Earth orbit satellites.
Neither the Navy nor Boeing shared any details on how the exercise unfolded or what was achieved, but, assuming everything worked as planned, we just witnessed something that, again, could reshape naval aviation operations.
The Stingray is powered by a single Rolls-Royce AE 3007N engine, and it has been designed to fly for a distance of up to 580 miles (930 km), either autonomously or controlled from a carrier deck or inside fighter plane cockpits.
In the tanker configuration, it carries a 15,000-pound (6,800 kg) aerial refuelling store (ARS) and a boom that allows it to refuel airplanes the likes of the F/A-18 Super Hornets mid-flight. It has been selected for this role as the Navy seeks to relieve said Super Hornets from their buddy refuelling and allow them to act in the capacity they were designed for.
Despite its new role, the drone still comes equipped with underwing hardpoints that can carry anti-ship missiles and can continue to be used as an ISR asset.
The Navy will continue to test the design in the coming months, using the seven test aircraft that are being built at the Boeing facilities in St. Louis, Missouri, and Mascoutah, Illinois. The company’s MidAmerica facility is involved in testing as well, and so will Naval Air Station Patuxent River in Maryland, where carrier qualification testing will take place.
Boeing is set to deliver the first operational drone in 2029. In all, the MQ-25A program of record calls for 76 of these drones to be deployed, including four engineering examples and five demonstration units. They will all cost the Navy $13 billion.

Rendering: New Bentley Flying Spur Gets Double Round Headlights and Torcal Elements in Some Places
8 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The ultra-luxury British automaker from Crewe, England, Bentley , has recently kept the headlines as it ramped up interest for the latest model release: their first-ever all-electric series-production model, the all-new Torcal.
Following its release, the company now has two crossover SUVs, the new Bentley Torcal and the ‘classic’ Bentley Bentayga with ICE power under the hood, plus the hybrid Continental GT grand tourer along with its Flying Spur sedan cousin. That’s a balanced model range, for sure.
However, that’s not all, because the ultra-luxury brand recently reinvented its showroom ethos beginning with the oldest Bentley retailer out there. Jack Barclay in London, established in 1927, is named after a racing driver of that era and operated by H.R. Owen – now it’s the flagship dealer for the new ethos.
Last but not least, we’re also seeing a new business strategy flourishing around the headquarters. Precisely, the all-new Bentley Torcal headlines a business plan that aims to keep both ICE and hybrid models in production for longer while the brand slows down its all-electric investments, and a new EV model isn’t coming before 2030, while the full-EV deadline has been postponed because now gasoline options are here to stay, most likely electrified to make them more powerful and efficient.
Anyway, it’s no wonder that the rumor mill continues to ask questions about the future of the Volkswagen AG brand, and just recently the good folks at Kolesa , along with their resident pixel master Nikita Chuicko, aka ' kelsonik ' on social media, imagined the next-gen Bentley sedan, the Flying Spur, going through a comprehensive digital transformation.
Now, though, the virtual artist is back playing with the Bentley Flying Spur, the modern incarnation, envisioning the fourth generation of the full-size luxury sedan way ahead of time, as the model recently went through its full mid-cycle refresh procedure. His vision, though, keeps the profile mostly the same and only works on the front and rear.
The ‘new’ Bentley Flying Spur returns to double round LED headlights with LED daytime halo rings, uses the new Torcal grille, and makes the sedan more muscular through the protruding front bumper or the more upright front and rear fender flares. Around the back, there’s a new rear style with slim LED taillights and the trunk separated from the wider fender flares like on the Torcal.
The red sedan is dressed with black concave alloy wheels to bode well for the low-placed black plastic body elements, and then the author also compares the new version with the previous CGI created for Kolesa plus the older sedan, along with the direct competition – Rolls-Royce’s Ghost. So, what do you think – yay or nay for a fresh take on the Bentley Flying Spur that’s different from the current 2027 model year? Mercedes-AMG F1 Drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli Go Off-Road in BMW-Powered SUVs
7 photos
Photo: INEOS
There's a certain irony whenever a Formula 1 driver gets behind the wheel of something a lot more rudimentary like an old-school 4x4. I quite like it. It speaks to their character. Anyway, that's exactly what's going on in this new INEOS campaign, where Mercedes-AMG F1 drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli got the chance to experience the Grenadier in its natural habitat.
The carmaker just released a new promotional video featuring George and Kimi behind the wheel of the Grenadier 4x4, each with their own build/spec of the vehicle. Antonelli went with a roof rack, hard shell tent, a Batwing awning and tailgate table, so that he can enjoy a little tiramisu along the way. This is what's called a camp-ready spec.
Meanwhile, George's build was a trail-ready spec with a recovery kit, rock sliders, a bull bar, and Gearmate drawers for his essentials, meaning his padel gear. By the way, if you purchase your INEOS Grenadier now, you will receive a complimentary kit of your choice up to £3,536 ($4,720). Basically the Expedition kit, Cargo kit, and the Field kit are all in play. The latter is a £2,376 ($3,171) option.
As part of the marketing ad, Russell and Antonelli are filmed taking a detour from the tarmac and pulling in for an unusual pit stop - or rather a 'Grid Stop'. That's where the Grenadier pit crew quickly mounts all the fitting accessories, camping kit and custom enhancements. Like I said, it's all tongue-in-cheek and meant to highlight how the Grenadier can be customized to suit pretty much every buyer's specific needs and preferences.
"The INEOS Grenadier is built for more, designed to give owners the freedom to customize their vehicle to fit whatever their 'more' may be. With a dash of humor and the two hottest drivers in Formula 1, the 'Grid Stop' film shows that customization possibilities are endless. We hope it inspires everyone watching to kit out their own Grenadier," stated INEOS' chief marketing officer, Jonathan Hill.
As some of you probably know already, INEOS is a major partner for Mercedes- AMG in F1, not to mention a one-third shareholder in the team. It's only natural that they would go above and beyond to promote this partnership. In fact, INEOS has been a Mercedes F1 partner since 2020, and while the Grenadier is closely associated with Mercedes through this partnership, there's something quite amusing going on here.
Photo: INEOS The Grenadier is powered by BMW engines. That's right. What you're seeing here are two Mercedes F1 drivers helping promote a vehicle powered by engines sourced from one of their employer's biggest rivals in the passenger car segment. Not that there's anything wrong with that. I'm just saying... it's amusing. Besides, the Grenadier was never intended to compete with any luxury SUVs from Mercedes-Benz to begin with.
This is more of a spiritual successor to the original Land Rover Defender, putting the focus on durability and off-road capability.
I quite like it. I didn't think I would, initially. But I've long since come around to it.

Mighty Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Drags Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 and It Was a Comedy of Errors
18 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a detour around BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida for some cool excerpts from the FL2K competition, but now they're back at The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.
So, after the intermezzo at BMP, it’s time to head back to The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway as the videographer caught a couple of traditional fighters that were ready to bring honor to their brands – or so we thought, at least initially.
First, let’s meet the protagonists. In the left lane resides a defunct Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat , which has a 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi V8 with various levels of power, depending on the exact model year and versions. This particular unit comes dark and menacing, but it also has contrasting elements: the silver wrap on the hood, roof, and trunk combined with dual black stripes, as well as the gold rear alloy wheels.
Meanwhile, its opponent, the S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 , is dressed in satin black and also has its own contrasting elements: orange trim on the brake calipers, badges, or the rear wing, among other places. Both looked menacingly sporty and ready to make their fans proud, of course. But looks can be deceiving when the drivers don’t really know exactly what they are doing.
And this is a good example of a comedy of errors: they lined up properly, but only the Shelby took off at the green light while the Dodge was still dozing off for one reason or the other. No worries, as the GT500 almost came to a complete stop a few feet in front of the Dodge, then accelerated again after seeing the Mopar take the point.
We thought it was over for the Blue Oval, but no, the comedy was still going on: the Shelby accelerated heavily and managed to recover the lost distance and beat the Hellcat to the finish line, as the latter looked like it was out for a cruise, not at a quarter-mile dragstrip competition. In the end, though, none of them impressed us following this major debacle: 13.37s at 121 mph versus 13.65s at just 99 mph.
These figures aren’t worthy of the Hellcat and Shelby GT500 names, for sure, right? Anyway, over on the streets, the Blue Oval representative is doing much better these days than Dodge’s. That’s because the Challenger is retired, and the eighth generation Charger can’t make up for the lost ground compared to the S650 Ford Mustang.
As such, during the third quarter of the year, the S650 absolutely crushed its Charger competition as far as the ICE models are concerned. Ford sold almost 10k Mustang units, while Dodge only reached 3,446 sales in the quarter with the Hurricane-equipped Charger.
